bullets: Game 5 of a six-game deck-showcase video (video 989.2s-1300.0s); a fresh 2.4-elixir Wall Breakers cycle list, different from the decks in the earlier games.

Wall Breakers do double duty: real pairs at the left-lane bridge ([5, 14] clock 2:43, [4, 15] 1:38, [2, 14] overtime 1:41) and pure cycle drops behind the king tower ([8, 0] 2:36). The bridge pair at t=1066 produced the game's biggest chunk, enemy left 4616 -> 4056.

Defence is a fixed package: Bomb Tower centre-left, then Fire Spirit / Skeletons / The Log on whatever the opponent added. Both opponent Graveyards (clock 2:25 and 1:03) were beaten this way, the first with no tower HP lost.
Against a level-16 Miner played almost every cycle, he never traded up - Skeletons, Bats or Fire Spirit on the Miner and the Bomb Tower doing the work, which let him keep cycling Wall Breakers.
Magic Archer is the only splash and sits behind the Bomb Tower ([8, 4], [8, 11], [8, 9]) except one offensive [13, 20] in overtime.
Regular time ended level; the game went to double- then triple-elixir overtime with both left towers under 2500 when the readable window closed at t=1300, so the result is unknown.

new_deck.rationale: An eight-card list averaging 2.4 elixir whose win condition, Wall Breakers, is also its cycle card, with Bomb Tower plus 1-2 elixir troops doing all the defending.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Every defensive answer is cheap enough that the deck out-cycles what it is defending: Fire Spirit, Skeletons and The Log clear swarms and Graveyard skeletons for 1-2 elixir while Bomb Tower, placed centre-left, absorbs the Miner and covers the Graveyard radius. Because nothing on defence costs more than four, Wall Breakers come back around faster than the opponent's building, and Ryley alternates a genuine bridge pair with a cycle pair behind the king tower to control which one the opponent has to answer. Archers and Magic Archer supply the only ranged damage, so the deck has no real counter-push - the plan is chip damage from Wall Breakers plus defensive value, which in this match traded evenly with a Miner/Graveyard control deck into triple-elixir overtime.
